cards.title: Every edge carries its evidence: import, port or wire, checked against the tree

cards.body:
## Summary
Atlas's 120 edges are hand-typed claims with no evidence field. Give each one a `via` (import | port + `through` | wire + protocol) and an optional `up`, and add a test that asks the Python tree whether the claim holds, reporting checked / failed / skipped.

## Description
The model's one content rule is that every entry cites its source (data/types.ts header), and test/data.test.ts holds files to the tree. Edges escape it: an edge is `{from,to,kind,note}`, so whether `cmp-hooks -> cmp-catalog` is an import, a Protocol the composition root binds, or an HTTP hop is unstated, and nothing checks it. Scraping the imports of the 43 modeled src/athena modules shows three kinds of drift that no test can see today: 26 of 70 py->py edges have no import behind them (most are ports, which is the architecture README §3.1 is proudest of, and the model hides it); prompt->catalog is drawn backwards (catalog.py:46 imports prompt); and daemon/server.py:1052 imports wiring, a channels->surfaces up-edge, while model.test asserts 'no edge runs back up the stack' against the model's own list. The card follows docs-sync's source-as-data-without-the-app (strategy A: pattern-scrape the source, no Python run), checked-vs-skipped-denominators (an edge with a .rs/.js/.md end is skipped with a reason, never counted clean), and machine-authored-documentation's declared-truth-boundary (an edge says what carries it, so a reader does not read an authored arrow as a call graph).

## Flow
- test/source-imports.ts: a pure scraper `importsOf(text) -> Set<dotted>` (top-level, parenthesised, local) and `moduleOf(path)`
- data/types.ts: `EdgeVia = "import" | "port" | "wire"`, `through?: string`, `protocol?: string`, `up?: true` on Edge
- data/edges.ts: annotate every edge; correct prompt/catalog direction; declare the server->wiring up edge with its note, or leave it and let the test name it
- test/edges.test.ts: the three-population check + up-stack check against the tree; model.test's model-only up assertion becomes 'the up edges are exactly the declared ones'

## Expected impact
A drawn arrow becomes a checked claim: the class 'edge the code does not have / edge drawn backwards / undeclared up-stack import' closes for the Python half, and the ports architecture becomes data a later pane or read tool can print. read_view's layerLinks `up` list stops being empty by assertion.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every py->py edge's carriage is stated and verified against the tree
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (26/70 py edges unbacked as imports, 1 reversed, 1 undeclared up import)
After: 6 of 6, guards green
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: Scrape (node, regex over `^\s*(from X import ...|import X)`) of the 43 src/athena component files against edges.ts: 'py-py edges ok 44 unbacked 26 skipped 49'. Unbacked include cmp-hooks->cmp-catalog, cmp-hooks->cmp-policy, cmp-hooks->cmp-ledger, cmp-hooks->cmp-approvals, cmp-lane->cmp-cli-harness, cmp-cli-harness->cmp-hooks, cmp-prompt->cmp-recall, cmp-prompt->cmp-catalog, cmp-daemon-routes->cmp-lane. Reverse: src/athena/core/catalog.py:46 `from athena.core.prompt import BUDGETS`. Up: src/athena/daemon/server.py:1048-1052 '# Local import, and the only one in this module: athena.wiring composes ...' / `from athena.wiring import build_local`. Ports: src/athena/harness/hooks.py:24 `from athena.harness.ports import (`; src/athena/harness/ports.py:3 '``athena.harness`` never imports a core *service*'. Also 108 imports between modeled modules have no edge (not a target of this card).

cards.title: Coverage ledger: every src/athena module is drawn or a declared omission
acceptance: coverage.test: every git-tracked src/athena/**/*.py except __init__/__main__ is covered by a component's `file` (exact or directory prefix) or by an OMISSIONS entry's path prefix -> today 141 of 184 modules are covered by neither (99 of them in adopt/, peer/, proving/, vitals/), so the test lists them and fails

coverage.test: every OMISSIONS path exists in the tree, carries a non-empty `reason` and a `source` citation, and covers no component's file (an omission that contradicts a drawn component, or names a deleted path, fails) -> a seeded omission of src/athena/core/catalog.py fails 'omits a drawn component'

coverage.test: each LAYERS blurb equals its README.md §3.1 row (the text after the layer word, continuation lines joined, whitespace normalised) -> today surfaces (no 'the halo') and harness (no 'an API engine ... ADR 0031') fail; after the blurbs are re-copied, 6 of 6 match

coverage.test: every part README §3.1 names that has a module in the tree has a component -> a halo component under sys-shell (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/halo.rs, ADR 27) and an API-engine component under sys-runner (src/athena/harness/api_harness.py, ADR 31) exist; ADRS lists 27 and 31 under their own H1s (data.test's H1 check holds them)

coverage.test: the coverage numbers are a three-way split printed by the test - drawn / omitted / uncovered of the total module count - and the test fails when uncovered > 0; COVERAGE (exported from data/index.ts) carries the same three figures so a reader and a tool can say 'N modules drawn, M declared out of scope'
guard: no system is added (SYSTEMS.length stays 19), so lanes.model's SYSTEM_KIND-covers-SYSTEMS and KIND_COUNTS cases stay green with the two new components inheriting their systems' kinds
guard: model.test integrity cases (endpoints exist, unique part numbers, every concept lights a component, no edge runs up as declared) pass with the new components and their edges
premise: examples/atlas/data/types.ts:35 - 'an atlas of a machine that silently omits the parts that were designed and not built is a sales brochure' - yet nothing records the parts that ARE built and not drawn

examples/atlas/data/systems.ts:21 and :46 - the surfaces and harness blurbs, claimed 'verbatim where they fit', stop before README.md:137 'the halo (screen-edge light, ADR 0027)' and README.md:140-141 'an API engine (`nebius` ...) behind the `ModelFn` port (ADR 0031)'
examples/atlas/test/data.test.ts:22 - the tree test asks whether CITED paths exist, never whether the tree holds modules nobody cited
src/athena/ - 184 tracked modules; 43 are component files; adopt/ (15), peer/ (15), proving/ (65), vitals/ (4) have no system and no statement that they are out of scope
src/athena/harness/api_harness.py:1 - 'An engine that is a function, behind the same round loop (README §3.1, §3.2; ADR 0031)' - built, uncited by the model
.ai/registry-map.json - atlas-data-and-app x docs-sync is a recorded deviation: citation drift the tests did not catch
cards.rollback: Two commits: (1) omissions.ts + coverage.test + COVERAGE; (2) the halo and API-engine components, their edges, ADRs 27/31, the re-copied blurbs and the README count. Reverting (2) alone turns the coverage test red with a named list, which is the intended signal; reverting both restores today's tree exactly.
gates_to_run: pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test
cards.runner_up: Pin each concept's `claim` against README §2/§1's own sentence (the invariants table and the ladder), so a reworded invariant fails the build - narrower: 17 strings, one surface.
cards.body:
## Summary
Atlas maps 43 of src/athena's 184 modules and says nothing about the other 141. Add a declared-omissions ledger and a coverage test so every module is either drawn or omitted with a reason, re-pin the layer blurbs to README §3.1 verbatim, and draw the two parts §3.1 already names (the halo, the API engine). Adopts the open stabilize-2026-10-16 finding 'Model the halo and the nebius engine README 3.1 now names' (M, backlog).

## Description
The model's header promises it does not silently omit planned parts; it silently omits built ones. Four whole packages (adopt, peer, proving, vitals: 99 modules) and ~42 modules inside drawn packages (harness/ports.py, api_harness.py, core/setup.py, daemon/tasks.py, connectors/oauth.py, voice backends...) appear nowhere, and no test can tell a deliberate omission from drift. This is docs-sync's source-doc-mapping rule 'the map is the real gate: coverage, not membership' and checked-vs-skipped-denominators: the atlas currently reports its membership as if it were its coverage. The omission ledger is data (`{path, reason, source}`), prefix-matched so four package entries and a few dozen module entries cover the tree; nothing new is drawn except what README §3.1 itself names, and no system is added, so the lanes drawing (another context) needs no new kind.

## Flow
- data/types.ts: `Omission {path, reason, source}`; data/omissions.ts: the ledger
- data/index.ts: `COVERAGE = {drawn, omitted, total}` computed from a module list the test supplies (the bundle never reads fs; COVERAGE's module list is a test-side input, the ledger is the bundle-side data)
- test/coverage.test.ts: walk git-tracked src/athena/**/*.py, classify, fail on uncovered, stale or contradictory omissions; blurb-vs-README check
- data/components.ts / edges.ts / adrs.ts / systems.ts: C-069 halo (sys-shell, ADR 27), C-070 API engine (sys-runner, ADR 31), their edges, the two blurbs re-copied
- examples/atlas/README.md: 'sixty-eight components' -> the new count (the coupled doc)

## Expected impact
The atlas can no longer fall behind the tree without a red test naming the module; an omitted package is a stated scope decision rather than an absence. Prose counts in other contexts' comments (Claims.tsx:18, read.ts:289, workflow.ts:16, DESIGN.md) go stale as words - noted for the coordinator, not edited here.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every module in src/athena is accounted for (drawn or declared omitted) and the layer blurbs are README §3.1's words
Before: 0 of 5 non-guard acceptance cases pass (141 of 184 modules unaccounted; 2 of 6 blurbs differ from README)
After: 5 of 5, guards green
Method: gate - the acceptance cases
Result: better
Gate: none
